name: Big Sur South Block 01 original 2 m bathymetry and derived terrain class

producer.name: CSU Monterey Bay Seafloor Mapping Lab

units.derived_terrain_class: original categorical cells, rough/smooth and depth band

native_depth_screen.basis: original native source-elevation cell screen; no chart-datum conversion, uncertainty or legal clearance

temporal.update_cadence: Static 2011 acquisition; monthly archive integrity and catalog check

provenance.access_service: NOAA NCEI archive of original CSUMB survey; same source as the terrain class
transformations: Opened SHA-256-pinned 2 m original ArcInfo depth and terrain grids, checked alignment and counted native source-elevation and derived rough-class cells without chart-datum conversion or target generation.

evidence.supports: Original Block 01 survey identity and products.
Producer metadata specifies NAVD88 Geoid09 and unresolved original use constraints.

Original 6895c639d38e73f9871e185c8e79b4a99db002c537afb18ebdb4396d0e417548 archive; 5,001,340 valid 2 m cells, 3,773,386 within nominal 200 ft of source NAVD88 elevation and 166,433 derived rough cells in that subset. Exact audit: dist/data/csumb-bss-native-source-review.json.

limitations: The original 2 m grid includes shallow source-datum cells, but NAVD88 elevation has not been converted to chart datum and per-cell uncertainty is not supplied by this exported DEM. Neither its 200 ft cell count nor its deepest/shallowest elevations clear a fishing spot.
The terrain rough class is calculated from bathymetric ruggedness, not an independent rock sample or fish observation.

The valid-cell envelope is not an exact surveyed footprint or safe route; a Piedras Blancas MPA snapshot lies to the south, but all current exclusions and the actual trip-date rules still require review.
Producer access and use constraints remain to be determined; redistribution rights, chart hazards and approach remain unresolved.
